scope: Public primary-source research and read-only local code; no skills, no server, no training

papers.title: Driving in the Occupancy World: Vision-Centric 4D Occupancy Forecasting and Planning via World Models for Autonomous Driving
papers.version: arXiv 2408.14197 v3; AAAI final proceedings also opened
papers.read_depth: Methods 3.1–3.3; task/metric definitions 4.1; tables 1–2; author detector/head/config
source_facts: BEV history encoder + memory queue + autoregressive future BEV decoder; semantic/motion conditional normalization; occupancy and backward centripetal flow heads.
Future decoder uses deformable self-attention, temporal cross-attention, and action conditioning. Source losses combine CE, Lovasz and geometry terms; this is not uniform NLL-only training.
Inflated GMO, fine-grained GMO, and fine-grained GMO+GSO are separate tasks; general movable classes are not per-instance actual motion annotations.

portability.mechanism: Reference implementation and matched protocol anchor; generic autoregression or ego alignment is already present.

counterexamples_and_limits: No direct numeric comparison across inflated and fine-grained rows. Future ego/action inputs must match M0.
Local source M0 forecasting transition predicts full next state; its queue with length 1 removes the measured t0 state after first future step.

papers.title: Vision-Centric 4D Occupancy Forecasting and Planning via Implicit Residual World Models
papers.venue: ICRA 2026; arXiv comments and author repository acceptance announcement verified
papers.read_depth: Methods III B–C; setup IV; ablation tables VI–IX; actual Drive_OccWorld detector and fine-GMO config
source_facts: Predicts a latent BEV increment, adds it to previous state, and feeds the summed state back into streaming memory.
Paper feature alignment uses semantic and ego-motion conditioning. Open-source fine-GMO config sets sem_norm=False, ego_motion_ln=True, memory_queue_len=1.
Future feature teacher L2 (TSS) does not show a consistent forecasting gain in the paper ablation; do not default to distillation.

code.local_modification_note: Local drive_occworld.py restores occupancy forward_head/return fields; V2 also has a local patch. The residual recurrence is unchanged from HEAD. Do not represent these local files as pristine author code.

portability.level: directly implementable temporal transition, adaptation required
portability.interface: future_pred: next_bev_feats.append(next_bev_feats[-1] + pred_feat), then queue the summed final-layer feature; detector lines 374 and following.
dependencies: Official old stack Python 3.8 / torch 1.10.1 / mmcv 1.4.0

counterexamples_and_limits: An existing full-state M0 transition cannot be made residual merely by adding previous state; that changes initial predictions. Function-preserving migration must be designed and tested.
This is an internal recurrent state residual, not the frozen-output residual heads tested in R2–R4.
The single-slot official fine-GMO queue still drops direct measured-state access.

papers.title: OccProphet: Pushing the Efficiency Frontier of Camera-Only 4D Occupancy Forecasting with an Observer-Forecaster-Refiner Framework
papers.version: arXiv 2502.15180; official ICLR title includes the/an; author code released 2025-10-01
papers.read_depth: Methods 3.2–3.4; experiments 4.1 and component ablations; UNetPredictor, ConditionalGenerator, detector history extraction
source_facts: Observed voxel history is ego-aligned. Hybrid temporal fusion uses scene, BEV and height views; conditional generator predicts all future features in parallel.
Refiner concatenates observed history with predicted future features, then returns only refined futures. It does not consume future camera observations at inference.
Dynamic kernel uses Linear(T*C, Tprime*C*T*C*k^3); direct C=256 port is expensive. Author code has leave_attn_unused=True legacy default with instruction to set False for new training.

code.local_modification_note: Two local compatibility edits in data loading/view transformation; inspected core unet_trans.py is unmodified.

portability.interface: UNetPredictor.forward lines 651–688; ConditionalGenerator lines 187–282; optional post_unet mixes history and all future features.
dependencies: 3D convolution, custom voxel pooling; SyncBN configuration
Compress C before any dynamic-kernel port

counterexamples_and_limits: A voxel encoder differs from M0 BEV tokens. Preserve M0 axes/decoder rather than transplanting the entire image-lifting pipeline.
Parallel versus autoregressive prediction is established prior art, not a novel claim.
Author speed/memory comparisons are against Cam4DOcc and cannot be imported as M0 costs.

training_cost.author_hardware_claim: Minimum one RTX 4090; example uses four GPUs
training_cost.first_epoch_cache_warning: Author README states initial label generation may take hours

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Decoupling for Efficient Vision-Based Occupancy Forecasting
papers.version: arXiv v1 method read; CVPR 2025 final publication identity verified
papers.read_depth: Methods III A–C; supplementary section headings and ablation discussion; author detector and V1.1 config
source_facts: Compresses voxel columns with learned average/max pooling and predicts 2D occupancy, height and backward centripetal flow.
Temporal refinement propagates current instance associations through flow and masks occupancy predictions; it is not simple advection of calibrated 3D probabilities.
Conditional IoU relaxes penalties inside object boxes and differs from ordinary native IoU. The height-filled representation changes shape assumptions.

code.code_interface: extract_feat/cumulative_warp_occ; occ/flow/height branches; downstream flow-based instance refinement

portability.level: flow/instance mechanism useful; full representation not recommended first
dependencies: Instance and flow supervision plus voxel pooling

counterexamples_and_limits: Do not switch to conditional IoU to claim exceeding M0.
One height per column cannot preserve arbitrary 3D fine occupancy topology.
New instance/flow labels change supervision; isolate them as an added-supervision experiment.

papers.title: COME: Adding Scene-Centric Forecasting Control to Occupancy World Model
papers.version: arXiv v1 methods read; final venue identity verified; latest author code commit below
papers.read_depth: Methods 3.1–3.4; implementation 4.1; forecasting comparisons; author UNet/align config/environment
source_facts: A scene-centric U-Net aligns historical and future occupancy coordinates to a reference frame and predicts futures in parallel; final predictions are transformed to future frames.
Its occupancy forecaster conditions a pretrained diffusion world model with a ControlNet-style branch and visibility handling.
Occ3D occupancy inputs, camera-estimated occupancy, and GT/predicted ego trajectories are different settings. They are not the M0 fine-GMO protocol.

code.code_interface: UNet.forward at line 187; reshape target T/height; align_source_coors=True and align_target_coors=True

portability.level: reference-frame parallel predictor adaptable; full diffusion route conceptual for current budget
dependencies: Generative route additionally requires DOME VAE/DiT checkpoints

counterexamples_and_limits: M0 already has ego-aligned attention, so adding generic ego alignment is not a contribution.
Full multi-stage diffusion training is a large cost increase, not a cheap head replacement.
Static-dominated Occ3D gains do not imply fine-GMO gains.

training_cost.cost_evidence_note: Values from arXiv v1 setup; actual reproducible wall-clock not verified; do not convert to H200 hours

papers.title: OccTENS: 3D Occupancy World Model via Temporal Next-Scale Prediction
papers.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2026, accepted January 2026 per author PDF header; publisher bibliographic page not separately verified
papers.read_depth: Methods III A–D; setup IV A; tables I/III/IV and efficiency discussion
source_facts: Separates temporal next-scene prediction and spatial next-scale generation with distinct temporal/spatial attention; ego-pose is an additional scale-zero token.
Uses a multiscale occupancy VQ tokenizer; four input frames over 2s predict six future frames over 3s on Occ3D nuScenes/Waymo.
Camera variant uses FBOCC-predicted occupancy; -O uses ground-truth occupancy. Default six scales reports 0.56s versus OccWorld 0.35s; only reduced two-scale variant is faster in that table.

code.code_search_status: No verified author repository found in bounded exact-title/code search; this is not proof no release exists.

dependencies: New multiscale VQ tokenizer (4096 entries, C128, factor8)

counterexamples_and_limits: Requires retraining/tokenizer changes and a different annotation pipeline.
More parallel spatial generation does not ensure lower latency at the selected model size.

supplementary_nearest_neighbors.title: WORLDMEM: Long-term Consistent World Simulation with Memory
supplementary_nearest_neighbors.read_depth: Methods 3.2–3.4, algorithm1, attention equations and ablations
supplementary_nearest_neighbors.evidence: Pose/time-aware memory retrieval and cross-attention preserve context outside a rolling generation window; memory may contain generated frames.

preferred_mechanisms.name: Persistent measured t0 BEV + latest generated BEV, versus capacity-matched rolling two-state memory
preferred_mechanisms.reason: Directly restores observation access after first rollout while retaining whole transition learning; matched two-memory comparator separates memory content from size.
preferred_mechanisms.novelty: Established memory idea; exact M0 comparison not found in bounded search, not a novelty certificate.

preferred_mechanisms.name: Compressed-channel history/future joint spatial-temporal refiner
preferred_mechanisms.reason: Can repair cross-horizon/shape errors while retaining measured history; architecture mechanism distinct from recalibrating final scalar scores.
